# ankra_aws_cluster (Resource)

Provisions a self-managed Kubernetes cluster on AWS EC2 through the Ankra platform (not EKS; see `ankra_managed_cluster` for that). The counterpart of `ankra cluster aws create` and `ankra cluster aws deprovision`. Provisioning arguments are immutable, so changing one forces replacement; add capacity in place with `ankra_node_group`.

Import by cluster id. The platform does not return the build arguments, so the first apply after an import adopts the configured values in place, without replacing the cluster: they must describe the cluster as it was built.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ankra_aws_cluster" "example" {
  name                  = "aws-dev"
  credential_id         = "61262ddf-72db-4745-9a77-2c19961cf2d5"
  ssh_key_credential_id = "0f0f4d7e-2f0e-4f5a-9d6b-8c1a2b3c4d5e"
  region                = "eu-central-1"
  bastion_allowed_ips   = ["203.0.113.0/24"]

  # Instance types available in the region:
  # `ankra cluster aws instance-types --credential-id <id> --region <region>`.
  control_plane_count = 1
  control_plane_type  = "t3.medium"
  worker_count        = 2
  worker_type         = "t3.medium"

  # Destroying a cluster that still holds persistent volumes needs consent.
  accept_volume_data_loss = false

  timeouts {
    create = "60m"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bastion_allowed_ips` (List of String) CIDRs allowed to reach the bastion over SSH. The platform requires at least one.
- `credential_id` (String) AWS credential id used to provision the cluster.
- `name` (String) Name of the cluster.
- `region` (String) AWS region (e.g. `eu-central-1`).
- `ssh_key_credential_id` (String) SSH key credential id to install on the nodes.

### Optional

- `accept_volume_data_loss` (Boolean) Send `accept_volume_data_loss=true` when deprovisioning, consenting to the deletion of the cluster's persistent volumes. Without it the platform refuses to destroy a cluster that still holds volumes it would delete, and `terraform destroy` fails with that refusal. Defaults to `false`. Changing this only affects a future destroy, so it never replaces the cluster.
- `architecture` (String) CPU architecture of the nodes: `amd64` or `arm64`.
- `availability_zones` (List of String) Availability zones of the VPC Ankra creates.
- `bastion_instance_type` (String) EC2 instance type of the bastion host.
- `bastion_subnet_id` (String) Public subnet of the adopted VPC the bastion runs in.
- `cni` (String) Container network interface. Defaults to `cilium`, the only CNI kubeadm clusters run; set `flannel` or `calico` for k3s clusters.
- `control_plane_count` (Number) Number of control-plane nodes.
- `control_plane_type` (String) EC2 instance type of control-plane nodes.
- `description` (String) Description of the cluster.
- `distribution` (String) Kubernetes distribution: `kubeadm` (default, vanilla upstream Kubernetes) or `k3s`.
- `egress_mode` (String) Node egress mode. A created VPC uses `nat_gateway`; an adopted VPC is resolved by the platform when unset.
- `etcd_node_count` (Number) Number of dedicated etcd nodes when `etcd_topology` is `external`.
- `etcd_topology` (String) etcd topology for kubeadm clusters: `stacked` or `external`.
- `etcd_type` (String) EC2 instance type of dedicated etcd nodes.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) Send `force=true` when deprovisioning, which makes the platform tear down the cluster's AWS resources without its usual guards. Defaults to `false`, the guarded delete path. Changing this only affects a future destroy, so it never replaces the cluster.
- `gitops_branch` (String) GitOps branch to commit the generated stack to.
- `gitops_credential_name` (String) GitOps credential name; commits the generated stack to Git when set with `gitops_repository`.
- `gitops_repository` (String) GitOps repository (`owner/name`) to commit the generated stack to.
- `include_dns` (Boolean) Delegate a DNS subzone to the cluster and wire external-dns into the networking stack.
- `include_networking` (Boolean) Install the Ankra networking stack (Traefik and cert-manager) for ingress.
- `kubernetes_version` (String) Kubernetes version. Defaults to the platform's stable version when unset; `data.ankra_kubernetes_versions` lists the supported ones.
- `nat_gateway_single_zone` (Boolean) Run one NAT gateway for the created VPC instead of one per zone.
- `network_ip_range` (String) CIDR of the VPC Ankra creates. The platform uses `10.0.0.0/16` when unset.
- `node_subnet_ids` (List of String) Private subnets of the adopted VPC the nodes run in.
- `retention_policy` (String) What deprovisioning does with retained cloud resources such as volumes: `retain` (default) or `delete`. Recorded when the cluster is created; the platform cannot change it afterwards, so a change is refused at plan time.
- `root_volume_gib` (Number) Root volume size of each node, in GiB.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `ubuntu_series` (String) Ubuntu release of the node image.
- `vpc_id` (String) Existing VPC to adopt. When set, `node_subnet_ids` and `bastion_subnet_id` are required and `network_ip_range`, `availability_zones` and `nat_gateway_single_zone` must be left unset. Unset, Ankra creates the VPC.
- `wait_for_ready` (Boolean) Wait for the platform to report the cluster `running` before the resource is considered created. Defaults to `true`; set it to `false` to return as soon as the platform accepts the request. Anything that consumes the cluster - a kubeconfig, a `kubernetes` provider, a dependent module - needs the wait, because provisioning is asynchronous.
- `worker_count` (Number) Number of worker nodes in the cluster's default worker group. Further groups, and in-place resizing, are `ankra_node_group` resources.
- `worker_type` (String) EC2 instance type of the default worker group.

### Read-Only

- `cluster_id` (String) Identifier assigned to the cluster by the Ankra platform.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the cluster (mirrors `cluster_id`).
- `kind` (String) Cluster kind the platform reports (for example `hetzner`, `imported`).
- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the cluster belongs to: the provider's `project_id`, resolved to an ID when it is a slug, since the platform shows a cluster only in its own project. Null when the provider sets no `project_id`. Moving a cluster to another project is not managed here; after a move the cluster is no longer visible in this project.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state the platform reports for the cluster, refreshed on every read (for example `creating`, `running`, `stopped`).

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# AWS clusters are imported by their Ankra platform cluster id.
terraform import ankra_aws_cluster.example ef8cf93e-1d97-4494-9de4-12ced709ffde
```
